previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with left leg pain, swelling, and redness following a skin injury a week prior, concerning for cellulitis. She also had a mechanical fall resulting in a right shin laceration requiring sutures. She presented with URI symptoms, including cough, congestion, and wheezing, along with gastrointestinal symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Flu testing was negative, and chest imaging showed no pneumonia but mild pulmonary edema and atelectasis, consistent with an asthma exacerbation. Cellulitis was treated with antibiotics, and her symptoms improved. Her HCV viral load was undetectable, and HIV remained well-controlled. Anemia was noted, likely normocytic with borderline iron deficiency, to be evaluated outpatient. She was discharged home with services, on a 10-day course of clindamycin, with follow-up planned for wound care, anemia, and chronic condition management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ F with hx of morbid obesity HIV on HAART, HBV, HCV, chronic 
low-back pain / former opioid abuse on methadone who presented 
with 1)dyspnea 2)right lumbar pain 3)subjective fevers 4)urinary 
frequency. 

#Dyspnea - hypoxia: SaO2 on admission 83%RA, was diuresed with 
Lasix 20mg iv bid for 2 days with resulting 48h fluid balance of 
-6.5L. Dyspnea resolved and edema improved. O2sat on RA up to 
86-91% depending on sleep/wake cycle. OSA and 
obesity-hypoventilation syndrome are likely contributors to her 
baseline hypoxia as well as her asthma. Given unclear O2 
baseline and recent lower extremity trauma, PE was ruled out by 
low probability V/Q scan (CT not feasible given iodinated 
contrast allergy - hives, dyspnea). Was previously on home O2 as 
outpatient but then declined, declined again during this 
admission. Admission weight 178.49kg. Discharge weight 171kg.

#Low back pain: Chronic but exacerbated during this admission. 
Restricted mobility due to edema as well as morbid obesity. CT 
Abdomen/Pelvis negative for lithiasis, pyelonephritis. 
Incidentally worsened degenerative changes in lumbar spine. 
Deferred further work-up and titration of narcotics to 
outpatient care.

#Subjective fevers: received one dose of meropenem in ED but 
then was off antibiotics given lack of clear evidence for 
infection. Did not have any fevers or low grade temperatures 
inpatient. 

#Urinary frequency: Going on for at least one month. Per Dr. 
___ reported similar symptoms in the past ___ years. We 
considered her abnormal UA asymptomatic bacteriuria. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
#Foley: Given need for diuretic therapy and patient's immobility 
kept Foley at discharge. She is aware of the risks and potential 
benefit. Please revisit need for this. 
#?Cirrhosis: Certainly at risk given HCV and HBV. CT Abdomen and 
Pelvis in ED incidentally showed nodular liver contour. Consider 
HCV treatment.
